All 7 tests pass now with `python3 -m unittest -q`. I fixed two bugs in `household/bills.py` and changed one test that expected the wrong answer.

**Code fixes in `household/bills.py`:**

1. **`split_bill` dropped the leftover cents.** It returned `[total // people] * people`, so `split_bill(1001, 2)` gave `[500, 500]` and lost a cent. It now uses `divmod` and gives one extra cent to each of the first `remainder` people, as the docstring says. The shares now always add up to the total.
2. **`due_dates` crashed when the dates ran past December.** It added to the month without moving to the next year, so November plus 2 became month 13 and raised `IllegalMonthError`. It now carries extra months into the year using `divmod(first.month - 1 + i, 12)`.

**Test change in `tests/test_bills.py`:** `test_three_ways` expected `split_bill(1000, 3) == [333, 333, 333]`. That only adds up to 999, which breaks the docstring's rule that shares add up to exactly the total. The old code passed this test only because of the bug. I changed the expected result to `[334, 333, 333]`, which matches the docstring and the existing `test_remainder_goes_to_the_first`. If you actually wanted the leftover cent dropped, tell me and I'll revert the test change and the `split_bill` fix.

Nothing is committed yet.
